title: Calendar: lists of [start, end] pairs
description: Records can hold lists of lists; the header says busy:[[string]] once for every person.
question: Which full hours (start on the hour, 60 minutes) are free for everyone?

toon.none:
The data below is in TOON.

TOON (Token-Oriented Object Notation) — how to read it:
- Indentation shows nesting; "key: value" is a field.
- key[N]{f1,f2,...}: is followed by N rows of comma-separated values in field order.
- key[N]: a,b,c is a list of N values; "- " starts an item of a list of objects.

<data>
date: 2026-11-03
people[3]:
  - name: Ada
    busy[2]:
      - [2]: "09:00","10:30"
      - [2]: "13:00","14:00"
  - name: Alan
    busy[2]:
      - [2]: "10:00","11:00"
      - [2]: "15:00","16:00"
  - name: Grace
    busy[2]:
      - [2]: "09:00","09:30"
      - [2]: "11:00","12:00"
working_hours[2]: "09:00","17:00"
</data>

Question: Which full hours (start on the hour, 60 minutes) are free for everyone?

Answer in TOON only (no prose, no code fences): free[N]{start}: followed by one row per item.

akd.none:
The data below is in AK-DATA.

AK-DATA (Arkadia Data Format): <a:type,b:type> is a header; (v1,v2) is a record whose values follow the header order.
<[a:type,...]>[(...),(...)] is a list of records sharing that header; headers nest, e.g. items:<[sku:string,qty:number]>.
{key:value} is a record with names; <type> or <any> before a value overrides the header type.
Strings are quoted; numbers, true, false, null as in JSON; /*...*/, $attr, #tag are metadata, not data.
A record with fewer values than its header has only the first fields; //$size=N// before list items is their count.

<data>
<date:string, people:<[name:string, busy:[[string]]]>, working_hours:[string]>
(
  "2026-11-03",
  [
    ("Ada", [["09:00", "10:30"], ["13:00", "14:00"]]),
    ("Alan", [["10:00", "11:00"], ["15:00", "16:00"]]),
    ("Grace", [["09:00", "09:30"], ["11:00", "12:00"]])
  ],
  ["09:00", "17:00"]
)
</data>

Question: Which full hours (start on the hour, 60 minutes) are free for everyone?

Answer in AK-DATA only (no prose, no code fences), with exactly this header and one record per item:
<free:<[start:string]>>
